issues.problem:
Round 6 wrote: '(1) Fix A leaves a Ctrl+D copy out of the higher sets only in its original's slot'. This is false against the code and a measurement. Fix A leaves the copy of a hidden part out of every higher set that already holds its original. A copy in a slot that its original's slot outranks comes after the original, so it is left out too.

My relabel6 (work/relabel6.luau, out/relabel6.txt) uses V1's S3: his box with walls 0.02, fillers 17 above 18, and a Pommel filler 21 under them and wall 13. A copy of filler 18 placed in the Grip or the Pommel slot (both ranked below Guard) gives:
- on the tree: mass +0, balance +0, every owned volume the same, the copy owns 0;
- on round 4's src, f7ac37d's src and my fixA_sameSlot mutant: mass -3.148e-4 kg, balance -5.5259e-4, filler 21's owned volume -4e-5.

The pin's own sub-case 'it relabelled Pommel' passes on the tree and fails only on sameSlot and lastOnly (out/pinrun6.log, split runs).

The sentence also contradicts two other round-6 sentences. E-S2.14's tests bullet (l.2490) and M3-notes (l.3729-3730) describe the MUTANT fixA_sameSlot, which the pin kills, as 'a copy left out only in its original's slot'. That is the same words (1) uses for fix A, a merge error.

SPEC §4.3, §5.6, §17.2, README, M3-notes' scope bullet and the plain words state the scope without 'only' and are right. Only (1) is wrong.

The other 21,628 are valid; the 1,858 + 120 split stands.

- V1's 13,522-case near-copy claim is still in SPEC §5.6 and §17.1 O11. Round 6 removed the same claim from §17.2.

- --quick runs about 29.5 s at about 20 % load, the same as round 5 measured side by side.
